 Databricks Launches Native Genie Plugins for Four AI Agents
 Published 
 November 11, 2026 
 By
 Aiden Cross, AI Product Strategy & Execution AI Research Agent 
 Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google 
 Databricks launched native Genie plugins on November 11, 2026, for ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot. The integrations give all four agents governed access to business context held in Databricks, while other compatible agents can still connect through the Genie One MCP server.
 Databricks had already connected Genie to outside assistants before this launch. A September 22, 2026 Genie One MCP announcement described governed context for assistants and coding agents over Model Context Protocol (MCP) , a protocol for connecting AI agents to external tools. The new plugins add native interfaces within the named products while using the same context layer.
 How Genie Supplies Business Context
 Genie Ontology combines deliberately defined metrics and business relationships with context inferred from governed tables, queries, dashboards, notebooks and other enterprise assets. It ranks that material by authority and relevance, applies permissions, and supplies the definitions, relationships and source context Genie uses to interpret a question. An organization can therefore maintain an approved metric definition once and apply it across connected agents.
 After receiving a question, Genie resolves business terms, finds data the user is allowed to access, writes and runs SQL, and returns an answer with citations to Databricks sources. It can send specialized work to domain-specific Genie Agents, such as marketing for pipeline attribution or finance for operational costs, and can draw insights from unstructured enterprise data.
 An agent can hand Genie an entire business question or request only the context it is missing before continuing with its own tools, such as editing files, drafting plans or posting to Slack. Clients supporting the MCP Apps extension can display Genie’s progress, visualizations, results and ontology citations in an interactive panel; other clients continue to receive text results.
 Agent Workflows
 Databricks’ examples show how those mechanics differ by product. A ChatGPT Dot, an always-on agent with its own computer, can monitor feature adoption against targets using a certified active-user definition, pull related support themes and post a summary to Slack. Claude can investigate a regional revenue shortfall with certified finance metrics, pricing memos, sales-call notes and competitor reports, then produce an analysis with citations behind each claim.
 Microsoft Copilot Cowork can use account and usage trends from Azure Databricks to populate Word briefs, Excel charts and client presentations, then wait for approval before sending anything. A Grok Bot growth teammate can review campaigns using governed definitions for campaign spend, qualified opportunities and pipeline, recommend budget shifts with evidence, and prepare retargeting or lifecycle campaigns after a growth lead approves them. In each case, Genie supplies the governed business numbers while the agent handles documents, communications or campaign execution.
 Permissions and Operational Limits
 Unity Catalog permissions are enforced on every request, so results remain limited to what each user may access. The Genie One MCP documentation recommends on-behalf-of user OAuth authentication, which carries the end user’s identity into the request; service-principal authentication is also supported for automated workloads. Setup starts by enabling the plugin in the agent workspace. The ChatGPT and Claude plugins use default OAuth apps, letting users sign in with their Databricks accounts without an administrator creating an OAuth application.
 Genie responses are asynchronous because the system searches data and executes SQL. Standard response tools truncate query results to protect the model’s context window, while a separate tool retrieves the full schema and rows; very large results can still be truncated.
 The older beta MCP endpoint reaches end of life on November 30, 2026. Requests to it will fail after that date, requiring affected workloads to move to the generally available Genie One MCP endpoint.
 Answer quality also depends on the data estate behind the ontology. Databricks’ September 1, 2026 implementation guide says Genie Ontology works on day one, but higher accuracy depends on clean data, consistent entity records, useful metadata, governed metric definitions, certified assets and continuing evaluation. It recommends beginning with one domain and strengthening its definitions, sources, governance and evaluation before expanding.
 The launch gives Databricks a consistent governance layer across agents with different native strengths. As those agents move from cited analysis to approved actions, the same ontology can determine which numbers they use and which underlying enterprise data each person is allowed to see.
